instructions: Two tools for the running desktop. AX reads and operates application windows through accessibility: it lists windows, returns controls as rN refs, acts on them, and waits with wait steps. GUI takes full-desktop screenshots and sends pixel input. Use AX for named controls, values, menus, dialogs, windows, and keys. Use GUI for pixels, canvases, dragging, and controls that AX does not expose; after one targeted AX find misses a visible control, use GUI for it. Send all desktop input (window activation, keys, text, mouse) through these tools, not shell input utilities or scripted accessibility calls: the tools check the target window before input and report what changed, and outside input makes their refs and diffs stale. After GUI input, read AX again before reusing refs.

tools.name: AX
tools.title: Accessibility

query.description: At least one filter; ANDed, case-insensitive.

actions.description: act: ordered steps; a failed step stops the batch. Wait timeouts total at most 60000 ms; an omitted timeout counts as 5000 ms.

allow_global_input.description: Linux click/scroll only. false forbids driver focus/raise and pointer/keyboard synthesis. Semantic actions may themselves change app focus. Unsupported uses reject the batch before input.

keys.description: One chord, e.g. ["CTRL","S"]. PAGEUP/PAGE_UP/PAGEDOWN/PAGE_DOWN. Linux named keys are case-insensitive, including KP_ADD, KP_SUBTRACT, KP_MULTIPLY, KP_DIVIDE, KP_DECIMAL, KP_ENTER, KP_0 through KP_9 and mapped X11 names. Use PLUS for '+'.

ref.description: rN element; wN for activate/close. Omit for keys/text to the batch target (focused window by default).

settle.description: wait: true waits until the UI changes after the step before it, then stops changing.

text.description: wait: text in the ref element, or anywhere in the window. select: substring of ref to select.

title.description: activate/close: unique window-title substring, instead of wN.

to_ref.description: select: range end; ref..to_ref spans text or cells.

window.description: wait: a top-level window whose title contains this, on the whole desktop.

app.description: App name, app id, or PID; use once, then window_ref.

cursor.description: find: next_cursor from a truncated result; send with mode find only.

mode.description: apps lists confirmed top-level windows (wN, title, app, active) and reports incomplete inventories; observe returns a tree or diff with rN; find returns matching rN; act runs actions.

observe.description: Returned evidence. act: default diff; explicit tree returns the complete window tree, full adds the full-desktop GUI screenshot. observe: default tree. none only with act.

read_text.description: Linux and Windows observe only: read one live root rN without input or a tree. The ref identifies its window; omit app, scope and observe. Offsets count Unicode code points. Follow next_read to continue; pages are live reads, not a frozen document.

field.description: value reads AT-SPI Text on Linux or live UIA, IAccessible2, or native control text on Windows; unavailable or protected text returns an error. name and description read those attributes.

root.description: observe: subtree at rN or the focused element.

window_ref.description: observe/find: window to read. act: omit when actions have refs, which name the window; otherwise sets the initial target for ref-less steps instead of the focused window.

tools.name: GUI
tools.title: Desktop screenshot and input
tools.description: Full-desktop screenshot and pixel input. {"actions":[{"type":"screenshot"}]} alone observes; {"type":"zoom","region":[x0,y0,x1,y1]} alone enlarges a frame region. Each input batch is checked before input and returns one final screenshot. x/y are pixels of the latest full-desktop image from GUI or AX full/screenshot, which return the same frame. type/keypress go to the current focus; click the field first. Batch actions planned from one screenshot; end after an action that may open, close, or move a window, then plan the rest from the returned image. GUI cannot address windows; AX activates and closes them by title. wait is one second with no observation, at most 20 s per batch. Errors return code and hint; gui_frame_stale means no input: replan from the returned screenshot. Example: {"actions":[{"type":"type","text":"hello"},{"type":"keypress","keys":["ENTER"]}]}

inputSchema.description: One screenshot or zoom action observes; otherwise run an input batch.

type.description: Capture the final full desktop; this must be the only action.
Look only: enlarge a frame region; alone.

x.description: X pixel in the exact returned full-desktop image

y.description: Y pixel in the exact returned full-desktop image

keys.description: One chord, e.g. ["CTRL","S"]. PAGEUP/PAGE_UP/PAGEDOWN/PAGE_DOWN. Linux named keys are case-insensitive, including KP_ADD, KP_SUBTRACT, KP_MULTIPLY, KP_DIVIDE, KP_DECIMAL, KP_ENTER, KP_0 through KP_9 and mapped X11 names. Use PLUS for '+'.

type.description: Wait exactly one second without an intermediate observation; do not stack waits.

settle_ms.description: Visual stillness: default 800ms, max 3000ms. Final screenshot stillness, not semantic success and not extra sleep. After wait, usually omit it. At the cap inspect the screenshot or use an AX wait step.
